brief: A contacts app as a social constellation — closeness reflects relationship, interactions glow

dominant_strengths: Strong metaphor: glowing orbs on black evoke a real constellation, giving the contacts list genuine emotional warmth and atmosphere.
Color halos differentiate contacts intuitively, with gradient auras suggesting interaction recency or intensity at a glance.
Distinctive concept that escapes the tired list/grid contacts paradigm and reads as a memorable signature interaction.
dominant_weaknesses: Vertical stacking collapses the constellation idea — orbs sit on a single axis instead of orbiting, wasting the entire 2D canvas.
Initials typography is tiny, low-contrast on bright orbs, and rotated/skewed unintentionally, hurting legibility and craft.
No visible affordances for navigation, search results, edges between contacts, or scale — behaviorally it is a poster, not an app.
fix_priorities: Distribute nodes radially around ME with distance encoding closeness, and draw faint connection lines for relationship topology.
Fix initial typography: upright, higher-contrast, consistent weight, and add a hover label with name and last-interaction.
Add interaction states (hover glow, pulse on recent message, click → detail) so the metaphor delivers function, not just mood.
Introduce clustering or grouping (family, work) via color families to give the constellation semantic structure.
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral and reflective land well via the cosmic metaphor, but behavioral utility is severely underdeveloped — it looks more than it works.
rationale.intent_fit: Conceptually on-brief but execution under-delivers: closeness and glow are hinted at, not yet legibly mapped to relationship data.
